<h3>Cómo se puntúa</h3><ul><li>Pasa los:
How it's scored

  • Jump the fences in order: a green arrow marks the next one and the scoreboard at the top says which it is.
  • Knock-down = 4 faults: if you go through without jumping or too low, the top pole falls.
  • Going over the time allowed = 1 fault for each second started. More than 2 minutes = eliminated.
  • Medal: gold with 0 faults (clear round), silver up to 4, bronze up to 8.
  • Press Jump about 2-4 m before the fence; the horse jumps as high as it needs to. In easy mode it jumps by itself.

<h3>Muros, setos y cancelas</h3><ul><li>:
Walls, hedges and gates

  • The valley's dry-stone walls, hedges and fences can't be passed through any more: not on foot, on horseback, or by car, buggy or bike.
  • Where a path crosses a wall there's a gap, and where OpenStreetMap has a gate there's a gate that opens by itself when you get close (wooden, steel, a kissing gate or a stile).
  • On foot, facing a wall or a fence you get Climb over the wall or Climb over the fence; with a hedge, Get through the hedge.
  • On horseback, press Jump before you get there: it jumps walls and fences up to 1.6 m; not high hedges.
  • In kart races, courses and bike downhills they don't count.
<h3>Pista de saltos</h3><ul><li>Entra a:
Jumping arena

  • Ride into the arena, cross the start (red flag on the right) and jump the 8 fences in order. Finish between the flags in the middle.
  • At the top: the fence you're on, the time, the time allowed and the faults.
<h3>Rutas</h3><ul><li>Cinco rutas de ver:
Routes

  • Five real routes: to the Devil's Bridge, Kirkby Lonsdale and Ruskin's View, Holy Trinity and Casterton Grange, Barbon and the stone circle. On horseback, on foot or by bike.
  • The yellow line marks the way; the yellow hoop is the next checkpoint (green: the finish). At the top: checkpoint, time and what's left.
<h3>Puentes</h3><ul><li>El relieve del l:
Bridges

  • The laser terrain has no bridges: the game puts them where OpenStreetMap has them, with their parapets, and you can cross them on foot, on horseback, by car and by bike. The Devil's Bridge has three arches.
